episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 28, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the spine for today. Physical AI keeps growing its footprint faster than it proves its economics. We'll look at two versions of that gap, one in a Southern warehouse and one on the Shanghai exchange. Then we'll close with the one corner of the sector where scale has actually turned into paid volume.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 28, 2026
episodes.summary: The thesis for today: private credit's surplus capital has finally found an outlet big enough to absorb it, in AI compute, at the exact moment the bottom of its existing loan book is repricing toward levels last seen in 2009.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 28, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: Broadcom arranged roughly 63 billion dollars to finance Anthropic's chip purchases, and it is backstopping the lenders itself, so a chip vendor is now carrying part of its own customer's credit risk.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 28, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and a hit by the thinnest margin. Last Friday I said the latest ten-year yield our reads reported before today's Fed decision would sit below 5 percent. I opened at two-in-three and eased to three-in-five on Monday.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: One standing disclosure before we start. Anthropic makes the model behind this show. Today's lead puts a rival ahead of Anthropic's model on an independent index. The second story concerns Anthropic's own model and its IPO. Judge the framing accordingly.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis. Kevin Warsh's first meeting as Fed chair turned a hold everyone expected into an open fight over resuming hikes. Oil is giving the hawks their inflation alibi. And the AI buildout has started eating the free cash flow of the very companies funding it.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the headline worth sitting with: the Fed came and went yesterday, and Bitcoin stopped almost exactly where the average ETF buyer breaks even.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis for today. Washington just started financing the scarcest input in the AI economy, firm power. It did so in the same week that private capital for that power got meaningfully more expensive. Watch how those two facts collide.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: On Tuesday, this desk carried TrendForce's preview of a record SK hynix operating margin near 78 percent. We warned that one quarter's print couldn't settle whether the memory boom is structural or just the top of a cycle. SK hynix reported yesterday. It came in higher, at an implied 80 percent margin.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the interesting product decisions stopped happening inside the model and started happening around it. Three control points moved: how usage gets metered, who can be cut off, and which channel the agent reaches you through. We'll take them in that order.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has argued that enterprise AI mostly redistributes existing IT spending rather than adding to it. The evidence was bundled seats at ServiceNow and Okta, a margin story at SAP, and consulting-mix shifts at IBM. Last night's earnings broke that thesis, but only at one layer of the stack.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: First, a correction. Yesterday this desk said we'd found no verifiable new release from the robot foundation-model labs this cycle. That was wrong. Google DeepMind shipped Genie 4, its latest real-time world model, on October 27th.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the two launch catalysts we've been tracking finally split apart. SpaceX's Starship hardware just got fire-tested for a landmark recovery attempt. ULA's Vulcan comeback flight slipped again, and the reason is something we hadn't reported before.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: The public discount on private marks has stopped being just a number on a screen. Now it is forcing actual transactions. And the stress sitting underneath that discount is increasingly resolving somewhere nobody can see it.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with one number. Sponsor-to-sponsor sales fell to just 94 deals in the second quarter, the fewest in at least a decade. That count comes from the law firm Foley's midyear review of exit data. It counts deals, not dollars, and it covers a single quarter.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: Wednesday's Fed hold came with two dissents in favor of a hike, and that hawkish vote now frames rates, crypto, credit, and the cost of financing the AI buildout.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 29, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. Four calls resolved this week, and one of them went against me.
